items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Dick Allen ... And my name is Dick Allen.

ctx.x: Johnny De-Draw. Better known as Johnny De-Droy, and sometimes Johnny De-Troy.

And it didn't register before, so I'll put the date down again. We're here at the Howard Tilt Memorial Library, the Jazz Archive, March the 16th, is right? Yes. In 1973. And your name? Dexter Thompson. And my name is Dick Allen. So, since the machine didn't work before, let's try and see if you can answer that question again as well.
It was perfect. I'm with you. Help yourself.

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...And I'm Dick Allen. ... [INTERVIEWEE] Just looking at you, you were kindred spirits.

ctx.x: When I went to high school, the professor, your mother's a solitary, your father's a good guy, you don't speak French, you're a disgrace to the French race. I thought I'm an American, I'm not a Frenchman. But that didn't do any good. But he was too good for boys, I went to school, he had no name. Just call boys, hi.

Let me get my name and Betty's name done. Betty, can you give yours? This is Betty Rankin. Yeah, and I'm Dick Allen. And I'm Tom Hedley Droid. So we all know each other's name and we have that on the tape.
Just looking at you, you were kindred spirits.
